candidates.description: Create a covering index on payment_allocation (invoice_id, allocated_amount, id) to enable index‑only scans for the allocation rows, reducing rows examined during the join query.
candidates.sql_change: CREATE INDEX idx_payment_allocation_invoice_alloc_id ON payment_allocation (invoice_id, allocated_amount, id);
what_could_break: If the index creation fails due to disk space or lock contention, the migration will abort.
MySQL may choose a sub‑optimal plan despite the index, yielding no benefit.
candidates.not_selectable_because:
this patch changes the database schema, and both arms resolve to the SAME schema: mysql://localhost:3307/mini.
An index is a property of the database, not of a worktree. Once green's migration applies it, blue is querying an indexed table too, so an interleaved A/B would compare two arms that both have the index and report no improvement for a change that may be worth a great deal. That is a false negative, and it looks exactly like the system working.
The measurement was NOT run. This is not a statement that the patch does not help — it is a statement that this harness cannot currently find out. Give each arm its own schema and run again; docs/schema-changes.md says what that requires.

candidates.description: Rewrite the payment‑history query to fetch the invoice header in a derived sub‑query, avoiding repeated scanning of the invoice table for each allocation row and thus reducing rows examined.
candidates.sql_before: SELECT i.amount, i.status, pa.id, p.paid_on, pa.allocated_amount, p.method FROM invoice i LEFT JOIN payment_allocation pa ON pa.invoice_id = i.id LEFT JOIN customer_payment p ON p.id = pa.payment_id WHERE i.id = %s ORDER BY p.paid_on ASC, p.id ASC, pa.id ASC
candidates.sql_after: SELECT i.amount, i.status, pa.id, p.paid_on, pa.allocated_amount, p.method FROM (SELECT amount, status FROM invoice WHERE id = %s) i LEFT JOIN payment_allocation pa ON pa.invoice_id = %s LEFT JOIN customer_payment p ON p.id = pa.payment_id ORDER BY p.paid_on ASC, p.id ASC, pa.id ASC
what_could_break: The derived sub‑query must return exactly one row; if the invoice does not exist the query returns no rows and the service will throw an exception as before.
If the optimizer does not use the sub‑query as intended, rows examined may not change.
